# Parity ledger

Generated by `uv run python -m scripts.generate_parity_ledger`; do not edit this document.
Edit your group file in `docs/contracts/parity-ledger-status.d/`, then regenerate.
All JSON shards merge in filename order; duplicate surface keys are errors.
Each entry is a status string or an object: `{"status": "proxied", "note": "Rust work"}`.
Objects require exactly `status` and `note`, both strings. Statuses are `proxied`,
`delegated`, or `dropped by decision #N` (a positive task number). Notes cite evidence
or blocking Rust work; string entries have empty notes. Pipes and line breaks in notes
are escaped for the table. Malformed entries are errors.

Exit rule: every row must be `delegated` or `dropped by decision <ref>` with a recorded
decision. `proxied` and **unclassified** rows block #21573, the S3.2 naming switch
with Python removed. Deletion child #21574 owns the mechanical deletion, gated by
this exit check before the switch.
The native terminal default flip has its own evidence row referencing #21357
Plan native runtime completion. A closed planning task alone does not prove the flip.

Sources: registered FastAPI/ASGI routes (including MCP and WS transports), inbound
WebSocket dispatch messages, built-in MCP registries, daemon HTTP /mcp tools,
the agent-facing stdio MCP bridge (`gobby mcp-server`), and
registered Click verbs (groups and aliases included). Registration uses inert services;
no daemon, database connection or handler runs. Deployment-specific external MCP
servers and UI asset/dev-server mounts are outside this backend inventory.
`HTTP *` denotes an ASGI route with no method filter in the parent route table.
Dropped rows remain as decision evidence after removal; other mapping keys must
identify currently registered surfaces. Unmapped surfaces are visibly unclassified.
Parity waivers in `docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json` cite a changed behaviour inside a
row; the row status is unchanged and the note reads `Waived`. `native-extension` rows are
additive surfaces with no Python counterpart; their readiness comes from native tests alone.
